I5.quote: Here, we report the fabrication of a graphene-wrapped nanostructured reactive hydride composite, i.e., 2LiBH4-MgH2, made by adopting graphene-supported MgH2 nanoparticles (NPs) as the nanoreactor and heterogeneous nucleation sites.

notes: I1: gas-phase H2 uptake is measured volumetrically (Sieverts): hydrogenation curves in Fig. 5a (main p. 6, 'dehydrogenation ... and hydrogenation for LBMH80@G and bulk 2LiBH4-MgH2 composite at 350 °C', 0-10 wt% axis) and PCT absorption ('Ab') isotherms of LBMH80@G at 350-395 °C in Fig. S9a (si1 p. 12). I2: LBMH80@G is 80 wt% 2LiBH4-MgH2 hydride on 20 wt% graphene (abstract: 'extremely high loading capacity (80 wt%)'; Table S1: 'Graphene 80 wt%'), so its majority component by mass is the hydride, not carbon (protocol §3: hydrides are not carbon sorbents); the bulk ball-milled 2LiBH4-MgH2 contains no carbon. LBMH40@G (40 wt% hydride, 60 wt% graphene) and LBMH60@G appear only in desorption of the as-synthesized material (TGA-MS Fig. 4a,b; isothermal volumetric dehydrogenation under 0.3 MPa back pressure Fig. 4c; volumetric thermal decomposition Fig. S6), not in any gas-phase H2 uptake measurement, so they do not satisfy I2. Graphene alone and MH20@G/MH60@G have no H2 uptake measurement. I4: the only surface area (BET 794.7 m2/g, N2 at liquid-nitrogen temperature, Quantachrome NOVA 4200e) is for MH20@G (graphene-supported MgH2 before LiBH4 infiltration), a sample the paper reports measurements on but not one with a measured H2 uptake.
